title: 美国宇航员45年来首次溅落着陆
desc: 美国宇航员45年来首次溅落着陆

paragraphs.en: A busy summer of space travel came to a soft splashing end this week for astronauts Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley.
paragraphs.zh: 对于宇航员鲍勃·本肯和道格·赫尔利来说，他们忙碌的夏季太空旅行在本周以柔和的溅落着陆画上了句号。

paragraphs.en: It was the first splashdown by US astronauts in 45 years.
paragraphs.zh: 这是美国宇航员45年来首次溅落着陆。

paragraphs.en: As we descended through the atmosphere, the thrusters were firing almost continuously.
paragraphs.zh: 当我们穿过大气层下降时，推进器几乎一直在点火。

paragraphs.en: And I think this the sound that makes, I did record some audio of it, but it doesn't sound like a machine, it sounds like an animal.
paragraphs.zh: 我认为这是它发出的声音，我确实录下了一些音频，但听起来不像机器发出的，倒像是动物发出的。

paragraphs.en: The reentry is a fairly dynamic event and you can see from you know just an overall view of the capsule that reentry is a pretty demanding environment, you know with the different scorches on the vehicle and the windows were not spared any of that.
paragraphs.zh: 再入大气层是一个相当动态的事件，从太空舱的整体情况来看，再入大气层是一个相当严苛的环境，飞行器上有不同的烧灼痕迹，舷窗也未能幸免。

paragraphs.en: The two rode a SpaceX Dragon capsule to the ISS and back, marking the first such journey aboard a privately built and owned craft in the space station's 20-year history.
paragraphs.zh: 两人乘坐太空探索技术公司（SpaceX）的“龙”飞船前往国际空间站并返回，这标志着在国际空间站20年的历史中，首次有人员搭乘私人建造和拥有的航天器完成此类太空之旅。

paragraphs.en: The mission's success means another SpaceX crew launch could happen as early as next month with possible tourist flights next year.
paragraphs.zh: 此次任务的成功意味着SpaceX公司可能最早在下个月再次进行载人发射，明年还有可能开展旅游飞行。

paragraphs.en: Also this week from Cape Canaveral in Florida, NASA launched Perseverance, its most elaborate life-seeking Mars rover.
paragraphs.zh: 同样在本周，美国国家航空航天局（NASA）从佛罗里达州的卡纳维拉尔角发射了“毅力号”，这是其最精密的寻找生命的火星车。

paragraphs.en: Research scientist Dr Bethany Ehlmann explains the mission.
paragraphs.zh: 研究科学家贝尚妮·埃尔曼博士解释了这项任务。

paragraphs.en: We will be able to as before with rovers drive up to rocks, investigate them, figure out which ones are the most interesting.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将能够像以前一样，用火星车开到岩石旁，对它们进行研究，找出哪些是最有趣的。

paragraphs.en: But this time we'll be able to then core a piece of that rock out into a sample about the size of a piece of chalk.
paragraphs.zh: 但这次我们将能够从那块岩石中取出一块大约粉笔大小的样本。

paragraphs.en: Stony Brook University professor Scott McLennan says, to best study the samples collected by Perseverance, the rocks must land back on earth.
paragraphs.zh: 石溪大学教授斯科特·麦克伦南表示，为了对“毅力号”收集的样本进行最佳研究，这些岩石必须被送回地球。

paragraphs.en: They're the gift that keeps on giving because the samples will remain.
paragraphs.zh: 它们是源源不断的馈赠，因为样品会一直留存。

paragraphs.en: Our ability to make measurements will evolve. They will get better and better over time.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的测量能力将不断发展。随着时间的推移，它们会变得越来越精确。

paragraphs.en: And we can always go back and revisit those samples that we've brought back to earth.
paragraphs.zh: 我们总是可以回去重新研究那些我们带回地球的样本。

paragraphs.en: Samples may hold clues as to whether life ever existed on the red planet.
paragraphs.zh: 样本或许蕴藏着线索，能揭示这颗红色星球上是否曾存在生命。

paragraphs.en: NASA and the European Space Agency will join forces to bring them back to earth around 2031.
paragraphs.zh: NASA和欧洲航天局将联手在2031年左右把它们带回地球。
